record.original_question: For first-order formulas over trees with equality as the only predicate, can negation be effectively eliminated from any formula that is equivalent to a positive formula; equivalently, when such a formula has a finite complete set of unifiers, can that set be computed?

evidence.quote: Can negations be effectivly eliminated from first-order formulas over trees, where equality is the only predicate?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the free term algebra (Herbrand universe) of finite trees over a fixed signature of function symbols, with syntactic equality as the only predicate. Consider first-order formulas built from equations s = t between terms using the connectives ∧, ∨, ¬, → and the quantifiers ∀, ∃, interpreted in this algebra. Call a formula positive if it is built without the negation connective ¬.

A substitution σ is a unifier of a formula φ(x₁, …, xₙ) if σ makes φ true in the algebra of finite trees. A finite set Σ of substitutions is a complete set of unifiers of φ if every unifier of φ is an instance of some σ ∈ Σ.

Question: Is there an algorithm that, given a first-order formula φ over finite trees with equality as the only predicate such that φ is semantically equivalent to some positive formula, produces a negation-free formula equivalent to φ? Equivalently, when such a φ admits a finite complete set of unifiers, can that set be effectively computed?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of negation elimination from first-order (syntactic) equational formulae over the algebra of finite trees has been shown to be decidable, with subsequent works refining the complexity (coNP-complete for DNF, D²p-hard for CNF). Hence the equivalent question of computing the finite complete set of unifiers when one exists has been resolved positively.

status_evidence.claim: Decidability of negation elimination over trees with equality was established.

status_evidence.title: Negation Elimination from Simple Equational Formulae
status_evidence.snippet: Negation elimination in equational formulae studied with complexity refinements.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent works establish complexity bounds for the negation-elimination decision problem.

status_evidence.title: Negation Elimination in Empty or Permutative Theories
status_evidence.snippet: Negation elimination is studied for empty (free tree) and permutative theories.
status_evidence.claim: Negation elimination is effective in the empty theory of finite trees.
